_comment: The New features carousel on Config → Overview, newest first. Moved out of dashboard-config.js, where the same English text also lived as fallbacks beside the locale files — 48 KB of the module, loaded to draw a panel most visits never reach. Keys are unchanged, so every translation still applies.

features.titleFallback: A search that finds nothing offers your finders
features.whatFallback: Searching for something that is not in your dashboard ended there: a line saying nothing matched, and no way onward without retyping the same words somewhere else.
features.howFallback: The finders you use most now sit under that line, carrying the words you already typed. Click one, or arrow down and press Enter. Brave Search comes with nextDash on ?B — and if you had already added Brave yourself, yours is left exactly as you set it up.
features.enableFallback: On by default. Include finders in search, under Behavior → Search, switches it off.

features.titleFallback: Shift+A opens the theme browser
features.whatFallback: Trying a different theme meant leaving what you were doing: into config, into Appearance, then into the browser.
features.howFallback: Shift+A opens it over whatever is on screen — all of your themes, searchable, previewing on the real dashboard as you move across them. Escape closes it and leaves the theme you had.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Press ! or F1 for the full list of shortcuts.

features.titleFallback: Statistics shows what the install already knew
features.whatFallback: Four things were recorded and never shown: how many bookmarks are pinned, when anything was last edited, when a page was last kept as a copy, and how long the longest-standing broken link has been failing. "1 broken" never said whether that was yesterday or March.
features.howFallback: All four are on the Statistics section now, and a new panel counts what you added per month — saying how many bookmarks carry a date, so anything saved before nextDash recorded one is left out rather than quietly folded in.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: Preview pictures come from nextDash
features.whatFallback: Hovering a bookmark asked that website for its picture directly, so the site learned you were looking at your own dashboard — and a site that refuses to hand its picture to anyone else left the card blank. On a real collection that was every picture leaking and two of sixteen cards empty.
features.howFallback: nextDash fetches the picture and the site's icon once and keeps them, so hovering reaches nothing but your own dashboard. The card opens with its text straight away and the picture lands on the card you already have open — it never waits on someone else's server.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — and you can switch it off: untick Image in the card's row checklist under Appearance → Display, and nothing is drawn, fetched or stored. Icons & previews shows what is kept and can remove it.

features.titleFallback: nextDash speaks Chinese
features.whatFallback: 简体中文 joins English, Dutch, German and French as a fifth full language — and it is the whole of it, not a partial pass. The dashboard and its cheat sheet, the command palette, the setup wizards, every config tab, the statistics, the health view and its reasons, and all 209 headings of the Help tab.
features.howFallback: Pick it under Appearance → Language. Nothing falls back to English on the way through, and the theme browser — a screen that had stayed English in every language — was translated with it.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — choose the language and the whole interface follows.

features.titleFallback: Search groups its results, and learns which one you meant
features.whatFallback: One letter used to fill the screen. Typing g put Gmail and widGetonderzoek in the same column, in the same style, in an order nothing on screen explained — and the ranking looked the same on your thousandth search as on your first.
features.howFallback: Results now group by why they matched: the strong ones stay open, the rest fold behind a heading and a count, and nothing is thrown away. The ranking reads how often you open a bookmark and remembers which result you picked for the keystrokes you picked it with, so mail can become your own alias for Gmail without a shortcut for it.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — open the search and type.

features.titleFallback: The search mode has a key of its own
features.whatFallback: Whether typing letters finds a bookmark's name or its shortcut was a tickbox under Appearance → Layout labelled “Interleave categories across columns” — which is not what it does. Nothing about the layout has ever read it, so ticking it to rearrange your columns changed how typing was read and moved nothing on screen.
features.howFallback: It sits under Behavior → Search now, called Switch Search Mode, and Shift + Q flips it from the dashboard itself with a message saying which way it landed — for the times you want the other mode for a single search.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — Shift + Q works from any bookmark page.

features.titleFallback: Every figure on a custom widget can have its own size
features.whatFallback: A tile whose numbers were all drawn the same size left you to work out which one mattered. The custom widget drew flat rows where every other tile gave its main figure room, so the number you built the tile for looked exactly like the ones giving it context.
features.howFallback: Each figure is now Normal, Large, Small or a Bar, set per figure when you add or edit it. The bar is offered on a percentage, where a share of a whole is something it can draw, and it takes its colour from the theme you are using.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — open a custom widget and edit one of its figures.

features.titleFallback: The shortcut letters are on, and have a third setting
features.whatFallback: The shortcut letters were on or off. On, they sat in a column of their own down the right of every category — as loud as the bookmark names beside them, and holding the width that made those names truncate. Off, you lost the reminder of what your own shortcuts are, and some dashboards had lost them years ago without meaning to.
features.howFallback: There is a third answer now, and it is the new default: the letter floats in over the end of the name while your pointer or keyboard selection is on that row. Nothing moves when it appears, and the names get about five characters of width back.
features.enableFallback: Config → Appearance → Shortcut letters on rows.

features.titleFallback: A search that finds nothing says where to look
features.whatFallback: Typing a bookmark's name into the search overlay reported nothing found while the bookmark sat on the page behind it. A plain query looks for a shortcut, not a name, and the overlay never said so.
features.howFallback: When there is nothing by that shortcut but something by that name, the overlay adds one line saying how many bookmarks carry it, and Enter runs the search the other way. When nothing matches either, “nothing found” stays the answer.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — it is how search answers now.

features.titleFallback: The browser's Back button moves through nextDash
features.whatFallback: Opening the inbox, health or config, or switching bookmark page, left no trace in the browser's history. Back stripped the address bar and left the view standing, so the URL said one thing and the screen another — and from a view, Back to a bookmarks page did nothing at all.
features.howFallback: Each of those is a history entry now, so Back returns you where you were and Forward brings you back. What counts as a step is deliberately narrow: a filter is not one, so Back leaves the inbox rather than walking through the filters you tried in it, and a config section is not one either, so Back leaves config the way Escape does.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — it is how the buttons behave now.

features.titleFallback: A triage run can be finished
features.whatFallback: The queue held every link the filter showed, including the ones already read, so an inbox of 5 unread and 35 read handed back all forty and asked you to decide again on work already done. The last card looped back to the first rather than ending, and promoting a link closed triage — clearing a backlog of forty meant pressing t forty times.
features.howFallback: A run now walks the unread only, with the active filter still applying. The last card ends it and says how many you went through. And promoting a link puts you back in the run where you left it, so one t clears the whole backlog.
features.enableFallback: Press t in the inbox, or use the Triage button above the list.

features.titleFallback: The inbox and health lists start where the rows do
features.whatFallback: Both views put a wall of controls between their heading and their first row: ten bordered summary tiles, a filter strip that scrolled sideways with four filters past its right edge, and eight action buttons across two lines. On a laptop the first bookmark sat below the fold.
features.howFallback: The tiles read as one compact line, the filters wrap so every one of them is on screen, and the actions you rarely use moved behind a ⋯ — Work through and Triage stay where they are. The two views were changed to match each other, so switching between them no longer means learning a second layout.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: A tour of what a custom widget can reach
features.whatFallback: The Custom widget can read any address that answers with JSON, which is the most capable thing in the Widgets section and the hardest to discover: nothing on the page said what it could do or where to start.
features.howFallback: Seven steps, opening the first time you visit Config → Widgets. It walks the catalogue of ready-made services, the fields a custom widget maps, and how a figure gets from an endpoint onto your page. Ask for it again from Behavior → General → Onboarding.
features.enableFallback: Opens by itself on a first visit to Widgets.

features.titleFallback: The server log says what it is doing
features.whatFallback: The log was a wall of lines with no way to tell a note from a failure, and whole parts of the server said nothing at all — a check round, a feed poll, an import, a saved copy, a scheduled backup, a write to disk that did not work. When something went wrong there was nothing to read, and when nothing went wrong there was no way to watch it work.
features.howFallback: Every line now says how serious it is and which part of nextDash it came from, in a sentence written for someone running it rather than reading its source. Detail level chooses how much is written — Quiet, Normal or Verbose — and takes effect on the very next line, with no restart. Activity trail beside it picks which twelve things are recorded in machine-readable form.
features.enableFallback: Switch on Collect server log to read it in the app; the container log has it either way.

features.titleFallback: A widget answers to the right-click and the keyboard
features.whatFallback: Renaming a widget or changing its width meant leaving the dashboard for Config → Widgets to find the switch, and the keyboard stepped around widgets rather than into them — they were the one block on the page arrow keys could not enter.
features.howFallback: Right-click a widget title for rename, one column or two, fold, settings and close. Arrow keys now step inside and move through its rows the way they move through a category, Enter opens the row under the cursor, and every action in the menu has a key of its own.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: A bookmark can stop reporting one condition
features.whatFallback: A link you have already looked at and decided is fine kept being flagged as stale, unused or broken on every visit. The only ways to quiet it were to delete the bookmark or to stop checking it, and both throw away more than the flag.
features.howFallback: Press n or z on a row in Health, or use its menu, to set one flag aside. The bookmark stays in your collection and keeps being checked — it simply stops raising that condition. The Ignored filter lists everything set aside, and one click puts a bookmark back.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: A widget folds away like the categories beside it
features.whatFallback: A widget is a summary, and a page carrying several of them has the problem a page of long categories has: the block you want is below the fold because the ones above it are open. Categories have folded since long before widgets existed; widgets could only be dragged, hidden or removed.
features.howFallback: Click a widget's title to fold it shut, or press Enter or Space with the header focused — the same gesture on the same header, rather than a second one to learn. Fold all, the . key and the fold-all button take widgets with them, and each block stays folded or open as you left it, per page.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: Statistics reports what the app already knows
features.whatFallback: The section counted bookmarks, tags and categories and stopped there. It said how many services you monitor but never how well they did, nothing about certificates running out, and nothing about how much of the collection has a saved copy — all of which nextDash had already worked out. Some of what it did report was wrong: the healthy share could read 100% directly above a row saying two monitors were down.
features.howFallback: Health gains uptime over the last day, week and month with the average response and the outages on record; certificates near expiry, counted per site on your own warning window; and how much of the collection has a copy kept here. Content gains a panel for everything that is not a bookmark — widgets, feeds, import sources, the trash and the automatic backups. The healthy share counts every state now, the cleanup score names the threshold you actually set, category panels show names rather than the ids underneath them, and the timestamp follows your 12- or 24-hour setting.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The uptime and certificate panels appear once there is something to report.

features.titleFallback: Adding a widget no longer loses the widget
features.whatFallback: The kinds you can add filled a whole screen at the top of the Widgets tab, which pushed the widgets you already have below the fold. Choosing a kind added something you could not see, and the only sign of it was a message in the opposite corner.
features.howFallback: Widgets opens on your own widgets with one button above them. The catalogue opens over the page, the way the theme browser does, and closes onto the new widget with its name ready to type. The Types tab lists every kind with what it does and adds from there too, and the Custom widget comes with twenty-eight services already filled in.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on.

features.titleFallback: A theme browser, and every theme rebuilt
features.whatFallback: There are 214 built-in themes and they arrived as a listbox of 214 alphabetically sorted lines — which puts a theme twenty positions from its own other half, shows nothing of what any of them look like, and cannot be searched. At that size a list is not navigation.
features.howFallback: It is a grid of cards now: one per family with a light/dark switch on it, so 214 becomes 107, with search, segments for light, dark and favourites, and a star per family. Behind it every theme has been given an accent of its own instead of borrowing the success colour, a depth layer so a card sits on a surface rather than beside a border, and an improved backdrop you can set to dots, grid, lines or hatch. Thirty-three new families came with it.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Depth starts on rich and flat is the dashboard exactly as it was, so the old look is one control away.

features.titleFallback: Three slow jobs, done to a whole selection
features.whatFallback: Rebuilding a preview, refreshing a favicon and keeping a copy of a page on disk were each on a single row's menu. A filter that finds forty bookmarks with no preview is exactly the case for doing them at once.
features.howFallback: Tick rows in the health view and the bulk bar offers all three. They run one request at a time behind a bar that counts, because each fetches a page belonging to somebody else. Saving copies asks first and names how many, since that one is minutes rather than seconds.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Saving a copy needs monolith installed; the run says so on the first row rather than failing forty times.

features.titleFallback: Your dashboard can show more than links
features.whatFallback: A page holds categories of bookmarks. It can now also hold widgets: eight kinds of tile reading data this install already keeps — uptime per monitored service, a thirty-day trend, what is waiting in the inbox, what you saved and never opened, which import failed, which feed went quiet, which certificate is running out.
features.howFallback: Add and name them under Config → Widgets, then drag them into place among your categories like any other block. Each has its own settings: which page it counts, how many rows it shows, one column or two. A ninth type points at any address that answers with JSON, so a service that is not in the list needs no code.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. A new widget says what it is for before you add it, and a tile that leaves rows out says how many.

features.titleFallback: Bookmarks that keep arriving on their own
features.whatFallback: An import reads a file once. A source is a place bookmarks keep coming from and is asked again: GitHub stars, Raindrop.io, Hacker News, YouTube and Mastodon. The last three need no token at all — a username or a channel is the whole setup.
features.howFallback: Config → Data & backups → Sources. Each source previews what it would write before writing it, remembers where it got to so a second run brings only what is new, and says what the last round did. The Sources widget puts that on your dashboard, which is where a failed import becomes visible without going looking for it.
features.enableFallback: Nothing on by default. GitHub and Raindrop want a token; the other three want a name.

features.titleFallback: A copy of the page, for when the page is gone
features.whatFallback: The health view tells you a link is dead and offers whatever copy somebody else happened to take — which for a page nobody else bookmarked is usually none. nextDash can now ask for one on the day you save the link, and keep one on your own disk.
features.howFallback: Config → Data & backups → Sources. Archive new bookmarks asks the Web Archive; archive.today is the second opinion for pages the first was not allowed to keep; and Local copies saves a whole page — text, styling and images — as one file in your data directory. Config → Bookmarks → Local copies lists what you have, grouped by the bookmark it belongs to.
features.enableFallback: Off by default. The Web Archive accepts captures without keys at a smaller daily allowance; a key pair from archive.org lifts it.

features.titleFallback: Tell the rest of your machine what happened here
features.whatFallback: Everything nextDash talks to, it talks to on its own schedule, so anything built around it had to poll. Now a bookmark added, changed or removed — and a monitored link going down or coming back — is pushed to whatever you have built: an automation, a script, a home dashboard.
features.howFallback: Config → Data & backups → Webhooks. Name a receiver, give it an address, tick the events it should hear about. Every delivery is signed, so the receiver can tell it came from your install; the signing key is shown once, in the answer to the save that made it. On the same tab, an MCP endpoint lets an AI assistant search your bookmarks and add one.
features.enableFallback: Both off until you set them up. The assistant endpoint reads everything you have filed, which is why it starts closed.

features.titleFallback: Search your bookmarks from the browser's address bar
features.whatFallback: Typing a keyword, Tab, a term and Enter is how every other search-capable site is reached without opening it first. nextDash could not be reached that way at all — there was no address a search could live at.
features.howFallback: Visit your dashboard once and your browser picks it up: Firefox offers it under Search shortcuts, Chrome and its relatives under Site search, where you can shorten the keyword to something like nd. A search now has an address of its own too, so a particular search can be bookmarked or shared like any other view.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on here — the keyword is set in your browser's own settings.

features.titleFallback: Every health tile leads somewhere
features.whatFallback: Certificates sat in a row of tiles that all narrow the list and was the one that did nothing when clicked — the count is hosts rather than bookmarks, which is a reason a reader cannot see. It opens the bookmarks on those hosts now.
features.howFallback: And Missing preview has a button that can empty it: Re-check and Retest all ask whether a link still answers, never what its page says, so the number could not move. Fetch previews asks every page for its title, description and image.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Fetching is one request per bookmark, so it asks before it starts.

features.titleFallback: Try a font size before you take it
features.whatFallback: Hovering a size shows it on the dashboard behind the panel, so you see the choice at full size rather than a word describing it. Until v1.3.3.2 the panel resized with it and the button slid out from under the pointer — with a mouse the size was effectively unpickable.
features.howFallback: Appearance, at the top: five sizes, each drawn in the size it sets. Point at one to see the dashboard take it, click to keep it. The panel holds its own scale while you are trying them out and takes the new one when you choose.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The size is per device unless you share settings across devices.

features.titleFallback: The add-bookmark form fits on the screen
features.whatFallback: Eleven fields under each other made the form 735 pixels tall, more than a laptop browser leaves below its tabs — so it scrolled and the save button sat under the fold. On a wide window the fields sit in two columns now: what the bookmark is on the left, where it goes and whether it is watched on the right, about 435 pixels in all.
features.howFallback: Add a bookmark with + or Shift+B. Pinned, the availability buttons and every warning explain themselves in a small bubble on the control, on hover, on focus or on tap — so a clashing shortcut no longer pushes the fields down as you type.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. On a phone the fields stay in one column and Icon and Note are left out, keeping whatever the bookmark already had.

features.titleFallback: Posts from nextdash.cc, on your overview
features.whatFallback: The project writes about what it ships. Those posts now sit in the overview's news stream beside the releases, so a dashboard you already open tells you what changed instead of you going to look.
features.howFallback: Your server fetches the feed — the page never contacts another host, and nothing about you goes out with it. The chips above the stream hide the site's posts with one click if you would rather not see them.
features.enableFallback: On by default, and Behavior → Privacy → Show posts from nextdash.cc switches it off entirely: the request is then never made. DISABLE_NEWS_FEED=true does the same for a whole server.

features.titleFallback: The hover card knows what nextDash knows
features.whatFallback: A preview used to be the page's own title and description — the same thing any browser could show you. The card now adds what only this dashboard knows: when the link was last checked and how fast it answered, uptime over thirty days, a certificate about to expire, how many times you have opened it and when.
features.howFallback: Hover a bookmark. Uptime and an expiring certificate show on hover, not only on a card you pinned with Shift+V — the health report is already loaded, so it costs no request.
features.enableFallback: Appearance → Display → Link preview cards. A checklist decides which rows the card carries, so a reader who monitors nothing never sees a status row.

features.titleFallback: Peek, pin, or turn the card off
features.whatFallback: Hovering gives you something to read: the card takes no pointer events and carries no buttons, so it never has to be chased. Shift+V pins one instead — it takes focus, carries Copy, Refresh and Edit, and closes on Escape.
features.howFallback: Three modes rather than a switch: Off, On hover, and Keyboard only for people who want what the card says without one appearing under the pointer. The hover delay starts calm at 250 ms, so a card does not open on rows you were only passing over.
features.enableFallback: Appearance → Display → Link preview cards, where the mode, the delay and the checklist sit together with a live sample.

features.titleFallback: One list for what the project is doing
features.whatFallback: The overview used to answer "what is new" three times over: a panel showing one feature at a time out of forty-nine, a release summary repeating the line above it, and the project's posts below both — out of sight on most screens. It is one dated list now: posts from nextdash.cc, releases, and the settings each release introduced, newest first, every row saying where it came from.
features.howFallback: The chips above the list narrow it to one source, or hide the site's posts entirely. A green dot marks what arrived since you last read it, and All news & features opens the whole list under About.
features.enableFallback: On by default. Your server fetches the site's feed a few times a day and your browser never contacts it; Behavior → Privacy switches that half off, and the rest of the list still works with no network at all.

features.titleFallback: The hover card says what you know about a link
features.whatFallback: It printed the address twice, left out whether you had ever opened the bookmark, and slid away as you moved toward it. It now answers three things in the same order every time: what the page is, what it says, and what you already know about it — whether it answered and how quickly, how available it has been, a certificate about to expire, anything newly published, how often you open it, its shortcut and where it lives.
features.howFallback: Hover a bookmark. Shift + V keeps the card open with Copy, Refresh and Edit, and Esc closes it. A line with nothing to say is left out, so a bare link is a short card rather than empty space.
features.enableFallback: On hover is the new default. Appearance → Display → Link preview cards offers off and keyboard only as well, a hover delay, and a checklist of the lines the card may draw — with the card itself beside it, drawn from one of your own bookmarks.

features.titleFallback: The button bar is one tab, not two
features.whatFallback: Where the bar sits was a panel on Layout; which buttons it carries were two panels on Toolbar & tabs, two tabs further along. Moving the bar and hiding a button on it were separate errands, and the second one was usually found by accident.
features.howFallback: Appearance → Button bar holds both halves: the five positions, each drawn as the page with the bar in it, and under them the main buttons and the extras with Show all, Hide all and a count. Toolbar & tabs keeps the header row, which is a different strip.
features.enableFallback: Nothing moved on screen — only where the settings live. Hiding a button still leaves its keyboard shortcut working, and :buttonbar moves the bar without opening config at all.

features.titleFallback: Save a link from your phone, or from any browser
features.whatFallback: Saving a link meant being at a desktop with the extension installed. On a phone, or in Safari or Firefox, there was no way in at all — you mailed yourself the link and dealt with it later, which is how links get lost.
features.howFallback: Install nextDash as an app and it appears in your phone’s share sheet: share a link and it lands in the Inbox. On a desktop browser, Config → Help → Inbox builds a bookmarklet carrying this install’s own address. The same route takes a plain web address, so a launcher, a script or a hotkey can save to it too — the integrations folder has ready-made pieces for Raycast, Dropzone, Ulauncher, Alfred and Apple Shortcuts.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. If this install asks for a password, set a capture key on the server and paste it into the panel — it opens these two routes and nothing else.

features.titleFallback: A link you already have is found wherever it is
features.whatFallback: The duplicate check looked only at the page you were saving to. The same link filed on Work went straight in again from Personal, and the duplicates report found it weeks later — which is reporting a problem rather than preventing it.
features.howFallback: The check looks everywhere now. Two copies on one page are still refused; a copy on another page is a question instead — “You already saved this on Work · Docs”, with the existing bookmark one click away and Save anyway if you meant it. The same document filed with work and with reference is a real thing to want, so the choice stays yours.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The add form, quick add and the browser extension all ask it the same way.

features.titleFallback: Link rot, as something you can watch happen
features.whatFallback: A broken link was only ever broken — not broken since May, not broken and never opened, not one of forty on the same dead host. And a page that answers 200 while saying “not found” read as perfectly healthy.
features.howFallback: A row now says how long it has been failing, the list can be grouped by site so one host down reads as one problem, a monitored check can spot the polite kind of disappearance, and a dead link can be pointed at its last archived copy with the original address kept in the note. Rot report in the toolbar adds it up: what has gone, what has moved, what has been failing for over a month, and what broke this week.
features.enableFallback: Spotting a page that says “not found” costs one bounded read per check, so it is a switch under Behavior → Status & health. The rest is on.

features.titleFallback: Ten links, two minutes — cleaning that ends
features.whatFallback: Work through is the best thing in the health view, and it was reachable only from a health filter, by someone who had already decided to do maintenance. Deciding is the hard part, and a filter holding forty-seven rows is a number people learn to ignore.
features.howFallback: When enough links want attention, a card in the corner of the dashboard names what is waiting — “10 links to review: 4 broken, 3 never opened, 3 not opened in a year” — and Start runs a session over the worst ten. It ends: it says how many you dealt with, offers another ten while more are waiting, and Done for today puts the offer away until tomorrow. Skipping is not handling, so the count is honest.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Below five waiting links the card stays quiet.

features.titleFallback: Fresh — the bookmarks that have something new
features.whatFallback: Today, Recently opened, Most used and Stale all answer a question about what you did. None of them could answer the one you actually have in front of a wall of links: which of these is worth opening right now?
features.howFallback: When a page you saved offers a feed, nextDash notes where it is while fetching previews and checks it on the background re-check interval. A bookmark then carries a small count of what has been published since you last opened it, and a Fresh collection lists those newest first. Opening the bookmark clears it — that is the whole of the read state. No article list, no titles: this is not a feed reader.
features.enableFallback: Off by default, under Behavior → Status & health → Fresh. Switching it on checks once immediately; the feeds themselves were already found while previews were fetched, so nothing has to be re-fetched.

features.titleFallback: The health list stays still while you work through it
features.whatFallback: Health asks you to open a link and see for yourself, and then charged you for it: never opened and not opened in 30 days each cost ten points, so the first open raised the row’s score and the worst-first order carried it away. On a list of two hundred that meant tenth place became a hundred and eighty-eighth, while you were still reading it.
features.howFallback: Usage costs nothing now — it is still counted under the Unused and Stale tiles, still named on the row, it simply no longer decides where the row sits — and nothing else in the order changes when you act on a row either. Where a filter does stop selecting it, opening one under Unused or re-checking one under Broken, the row keeps its place, dimmed and marked handled, until you change the filter, sort or search, or reload the report.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The score breakdown behind the badge now separates what costs points from what is only worth knowing.

features.titleFallback: Typing filters; Enter opens
features.whatFallback: A bookmark shortcut fired the moment what you had typed matched it exactly, so an ordinary word was swallowed halfway through: "invoice" opened something at "in" and left "voice" behind. Words starting with g, j or k lost their first letter to the grid keys instead. Which of your words survived depended on which other bookmarks you happened to own, and changed every time you added one.
features.howFallback: Nothing opens by itself any more. The list narrows as you type and Enter opens the top result, with an exact shortcut match leading the list — so a shortcut costs one keystroke more and behaves the same tomorrow as today. Letters only reach the grid once a row is selected, and the line you type into now shows the key that started it: > for search, : for commands, ? for the finders, with an × to clear.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. A short key legend appears under the bookmarks after your first keystroke and goes again when you open something — switch it off under Behavior → General, where shortcut hints on the toolbar icons now start off as well.

features.titleFallback: A failed check says why, and one miss is not an outage
features.whatFallback: A name that would not resolve, a connection that timed out and one that was refused were all stored the same way — not up, no code — so the outage list, the timeline and the export showed no cause at all for anything that was not an HTTP error. And a single dropped check counted as downtime for a month afterwards.
features.howFallback: Every failure records what went wrong — DNS, timeout, refused, TLS, content — and shows it wherever the outage appears. A failed check is tried once more five seconds later and only written down if it fails again. A recovery says how long it was down, a 30-day figure says how much history is actually behind it, and certificate warnings now come from every check rather than only from bookmarks set to Monitor.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The trend chart can draw broken, stale, unchecked or the score instead of only healthy, a whole selection can be muted at once, and the three-second limit on a check is now a setting under Behavior → Status & health.

features.titleFallback: The inbox counts what you can see
features.whatFallback: A search or a site filter narrowed the list and left the tiles, the pills and the badge counting everything, so the numbers on screen described a different set of links than the one in front of you. Mark all read reached links you could not see, and a sleeping link was invisible until the day it came back.
features.howFallback: Every count follows the filter, the button becomes Mark shown read while something is narrowing the view, and a line under the list says how many links are asleep and when the first one wakes. A link you marked read by mistake can go back to unread, and the page description sits under the title.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Import now sits beside the CSV and JSON exports: it skips links that are already there and says afterwards how many arrived, how many were already in and how many did not fit.

features.titleFallback: A category can span several columns
features.whatFallback: A category with forty bookmarks in it towered over everything beside it, and everything past the items-per-category limit sat behind a "+ N more" you had to click every visit. One long category was enough to make a page feel lopsided.
features.howFallback: Let a category spread and its bookmarks run across two or three columns instead of down one, at the same height as the blocks around it. How many columns it takes is not something you set: it follows from the items-per-category limit and how many bookmarks are in it, so it grows and shrinks with the category and never goes wider than the grid.
features.enableFallback: Right-click a category header and pick Spread across columns, or press Shift+W on it. Pages & tags → Categories has the same switch on every row. It needs an items-per-category limit — spreading is unavailable while that is set to Unlimited.

features.titleFallback: A way back out of a bulk delete
features.whatFallback: Removing fifteen bookmarks at once had no way back except digging them out of the trash one at a time. And if the save did not go through, the rows disappeared from the screen anyway with nothing to tell you they were still there.
features.howFallback: The toast now offers Undo for eight seconds and puts every bookmark back in the position it held. A delete that fails puts them back on its own and says so. The trash still catches everything for 30 days after that.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Tick some rows with x, or Alt-click them, and Delete asks once for the whole set.

features.titleFallback: Right-click a row in Bookmarks
features.whatFallback: Everything you can do to a bookmark here was spread across the buttons on the row and the toolbar above the list, and which of them applied to the row you were pointing at was not always obvious.
features.howFallback: Right-click any row for one menu on that row: open it, copy the address, edit, move it to another page or category, change how often it is checked, pin it, or delete it. Right-click a row that is part of a selection and the menu switches to the whole selection, with the count named.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Shift and right-click still gives you the browser menu.

features.titleFallback: Config → Bookmarks finally has settings
features.whatFallback: Every choice this section made was made for you and could not be changed: the sort reset on every visit, fifty rows loaded at a time whatever your screen, and a quick-added bookmark always arrived unchecked, unpinned and without a category.
features.howFallback: Ten settings of its own, including what a quick-added bookmark starts with, the interval a bookmark gets when you switch it to Monitor, how many rows a delete has to touch before it asks, what counts as "not opened in a while", and which archive service the archive links point at.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Every setting starts at exactly the value that used to be fixed, so nothing changes until you change it.

features.titleFallback: Ask when you added something, or last opened it
features.whatFallback: nextDash records when you add a bookmark, when you last opened it and how often — and none of it could be reached from the search bar or from a collection of your own. "Added this month and never opened since" was not a question you could ask.
features.howFallback: Search takes added: and opened: with today, week, month or year — and opened:never. Your own collections can now use pinned, untagged, days since last opened and days since last changed, and a Recently added collection answers the one question the others never could.
features.enableFallback: The search filters work straight away. Recently added is off until you switch it on, and takes its own limit and pages.

features.titleFallback: Four more things you can do without the mouse
features.whatFallback: Pinning, sharing, opening a bookmark in Health and filtering to a tag you can see all needed the mouse or the command palette, in an app where everything else on a row has a key.
features.howFallback: Shift + P pins, Shift + S shares, Shift + R opens the row in Health, and t filters to its tag. Ctrl/Cmd + Enter opens a bookmark in a new tab for that press alone, whatever your standing preference says. Pin also has a right-click entry now.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Press ! or F1 for the full list, which is also on the printable cheat sheet.

features.titleFallback: Tags on the bookmark rows themselves
features.whatFallback: Every row already carried its tags and showed none of them, so the one place you could not act on a bookmark’s tag was the row in front of you.
features.howFallback: Switch on tags in the grid and the first two appear on the row, with the rest collapsing into a count. They give way before the bookmark name does, and stay out of the way on a phone.
features.enableFallback: Off by default, under Appearance → Display. Category headers also give back their width: the sort in use stays in front and the rest move behind a ⋯.

features.titleFallback: Tags on inbox links, at last
features.whatFallback: Links saved with tags — from the browser extension, or captured with a tag already on them — kept those tags and showed you none of them. You could not see them, change them, or search for them.
features.howFallback: Tags now sit on the row. Click one to see only that tag, and click it again to go back. Right-click a link and choose Tags to edit them, search matches them along with the title and note, and both the CSV and JSON exports carry them.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Any link that already had tags shows them from now on.

features.titleFallback: How much of the Inbox you actually use
features.whatFallback: An inbox is easy to fill and easy to stop emptying. Whether the links you save become bookmarks or quietly pile up was not something the view could tell you.
features.howFallback: The Stats button in the Inbox toolbar shows how many links you have added, promoted and deleted, what share of the ones you decided on became bookmarks, and how long a link sits there before you deal with it.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The figures cover the whole life of your inbox.

features.titleFallback: Watch a bookmark, not just check it
features.whatFallback: A status check told you a link was broken the next time you happened to look. It could not tell you a site had been down all night, how often it goes down, or that its certificate expires on Friday.
features.howFallback: Press c on a row in Health and choose Monitor. The server then checks it on its own interval, whether or not you have the dashboard open, and the row grows a heartbeat, an uptime percentage and an outage history. Say what "up" means for that page with a keyword or specific status codes, watch for it quietly turning into a different page, and get an alert on Slack, Telegram, Pushover and others when it goes down.
features.enableFallback: Per bookmark, from the Health view. Alerts, check cadence and maintenance windows live on this tab.

features.titleFallback: Clear the Health list one bookmark at a time
features.whatFallback: Filtering to Broken tells you what is wrong and then leaves every fix costing the same three moves: find the row again after the list redraws, aim at its action, decide.
features.howFallback: Open Health and press f, or use the Work through button. One bookmark fills the screen with its actions large — re-check, open, delete, skip — and j and k move between them. Esc leaves you on the row you had reached, so dipping in for three fixes and back out is not a mode switch.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. It works on whatever the current filter shows.

features.titleFallback: Try a theme on before you keep it
features.whatFallback: Finding out what a theme looked like meant switching to it, then switching back if you did not like it — and doing that again for the next one.
features.howFallback: Open the Theme list under Appearance and move through it: the dashboard behind takes on each theme as you go. Press Esc or click away and you are back where you started. There are 23 new themes to look through as well.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Your choice is only saved once you pick one.

features.titleFallback: Read the server log without leaving nextDash
features.whatFallback: When something went wrong there was nothing to look at. Finding out why an import failed or a link check never ran meant reaching the machine nextDash runs on.
features.howFallback: Data & backups › Server log lists what the server has been doing, keeps itself up to date every few seconds if you want, and colours warnings and errors so they are easy to spot. Search looks through everything kept.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Limit it by age or by number of entries, and clear the whole lot whenever you like.

features.titleFallback: Search finds every setting, not just the ones you have seen
features.whatFallback: Looking for “webhook” found nothing at all unless you happened to have opened that tab before, which is the opposite of what a search is for.
features.howFallback: Every setting is searchable the moment you open Config, and settings answer to more than their exact label — “uptime”, “wallpaper” and “hotkey” each find the right one even though those words are nowhere on screen.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K anywhere in Config, or use Find settings under the section list.

features.titleFallback: See what you have changed from the standard
features.whatFallback: Working out why your dashboard behaves differently from the guide meant opening every tab and looking for a ↺ beside each setting.
features.howFallback: At a glance now says how many settings differ from the standard and takes you to them. Each tab of settings gained Only changed, and each group a Reset panel that puts the whole lot back at once.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The line stays out of the way while everything is still standard.

features.titleFallback: Every “show this button” box sits with the thing it controls
features.whatFallback: Thirteen near-identical “Show the … button” tick boxes in a row, with no way to tell which meant the strip at the top and which the bar at the bottom.
features.howFallback: The header strip keeps its group under Toolbar & tabs; the two halves of the button bar sit on the Button bar tab, under the control that says where the bar goes. Each group has Show all and Hide all with a count of what is showing.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — the settings themselves are unchanged, only how they are arranged.

features.titleFallback: The inbox explains itself, and its numbers add up
features.whatFallback: A snoozed link is hidden from the list but was still counted above it, so a tile reading 12 could open a list of 9 with nothing explaining the gap.
features.howFallback: Every count now means what you can act on right now, every pill carries its own, and a sentence under the toolbar says what the active filter selects. The ℹ beside Triage covers snoozing, promoting and the rest.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. An empty list now says which kind of empty it is, and long inboxes load as you scroll rather than a page per click.

features.titleFallback: See how the whole collection is doing
features.whatFallback: The health view could describe one bookmark in detail and the whole set barely at all: twenty monitors meant twenty heartbeats and no answer to how the week went.
features.howFallback: The Monitored filter now opens with pooled uptime across every monitor, the least available ones, anything slower than last week, and every outage. The header draws the share of healthy bookmarks over the last 90 days.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on, though the panel needs something monitored to describe. The trend line starts once you have opened the health view on two separate days.

features.titleFallback: Decide how much room the grid gives away
features.whatFallback: The gap between category rows and the empty band down both edges were both fixed, and on a wide screen they added up to a lot of nothing.
features.howFallback: Config → Appearance → Layout now has Category spacing and Page margins, each with Snug, Balanced and Airy.
features.enableFallback: Page margins start exactly where they always were. Category spacing is a little tighter than before — pick Airy for the old gap.

features.titleFallback: Deleted pages and categories come back
features.whatFallback: Deleting a page took its bookmarks with it and kept nothing anywhere, so the more one click destroyed, the less you could recover.
features.howFallback: Both now go to the trash for 30 days. A page is one entry — listed as “Page · 12 bookmarks” — and restoring brings the page, its categories and its bookmarks back in a single action.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. The delete toast also offers Undo for eight seconds, and a page returns to its original slot rather than as a copy nothing points at.

features.titleFallback: Add a category from the grid itself
features.whatFallback: Making a category meant going into Config or through the bookmark form — both things you did on the way to something else.
features.howFallback: A + sits beside the A–Z / Rec chips in a category header, and holding c does the same from the keyboard. Both act on the page on screen, so neither asks which page you meant.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Right-click a category header to rename or delete it, and a category you just made stays visible even with “hide empty categories” on.

features.titleFallback: Make a page from the pages overview
features.whatFallback: Adding a page lived in Config, away from the list of pages you were already looking at.
features.howFallback: Press , for the overview and use the New page row under the list — by click, by n, or by arrowing one stop past the last page.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Creating takes you straight to the new page, which is where its first category gets added anyway.

features.titleFallback: Fix a whole list of broken links at once
features.whatFallback: Health lists exactly what a clear-out starts from — broken, duplicate, stale — and then made you repair them one row at a time.
features.howFallback: Tick the box on any row, or press x to tick the one under the cursor and move on, X for everything the filter shows. A bar appears above the list with Set checking, Re-check, Open, Copy links and Delete.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Deletes go to the trash, and a row that changed since the report was built is skipped rather than deleted.

features.titleFallback: Tag several bookmarks at once
features.whatFallback: Tagging worked one bookmark at a time, so putting the same tag on eight rows meant eight rounds.
features.howFallback: Select some rows and press the toolbar’s Tags button. Every tag you already use is listed, with a tick when the whole selection has it and “on 2 of 3” when only some do.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. Clicking a tag the whole selection already has takes it off instead; setting a category lives in the Move button beside it.

features.titleFallback: Make a page or category while adding a bookmark
features.whatFallback: Filing a bookmark somewhere that did not exist yet meant leaving the half-filled form, making the page or category in Config, and starting over.
features.howFallback: Both dropdowns in the bookmark form lead with ➕ New page… and ➕ New category…. Picking one swaps the dropdown for a name box, and the new page or category is selected when you come back.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. A category is made on whichever page the form is pointing at, including one you created moments earlier.

features.titleFallback: Select several bookmarks with x and X
features.whatFallback: Bulk move and bulk delete used to live in the tag filter, so acting on several bookmarks meant they had to share a tag. Any rows will do now — x ticks one, X takes a whole category.
features.howFallback: Press x to tick the row under the cursor, X for the whole category, Shift+↑/↓ for a range, Ctrl/Cmd+A for everything on screen — or Alt+click and Shift+click with the mouse. Select is in the right-click menu too.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on. A toolbar appears with Move, Open, Copy links and Delete; Escape clears the selection.

features.titleFallback: Deleted bookmarks are recoverable
features.whatFallback: Deleting a bookmark used to be final. It now goes to a trash and stays there for 30 days before going for good.
features.howFallback: Restore puts a bookmark back on its own page at its old position. Delete forever and Empty trash clear it early.
features.enableFallback: On by default, and it covers every delete — including a bulk delete of twenty rows at once. Under Config → Data & backups → Trash.

features.titleFallback: Right-click a health row
features.whatFallback: The nine actions behind a health row’s More button were reachable only by hovering the row and finding the button.
features.howFallback: Right-click any row in the Health view to open that same menu at the cursor, the way a bookmark on the dashboard already did. Shift and right-click still gives you the browser’s own menu.
features.enableFallback: Nothing to switch on — it is simply there. The ⋯ button and the m key keep working as before.

features.titleFallback: Monitored bookmarks stand out
features.whatFallback: A bookmark set to Monitor now shows its status on the dashboard, the way a Periodic one always did — and you can say how much it should stand out.
features.howFallback: Right-click a bookmark and pick Show in Health to jump straight to its row, from the dashboard or from Config → Bookmarks.
features.enableFallback: Set to draw the eye only when something is down. Choose Always or Never under Config → Behavior → Status & health.

features.titleFallback: Button bar position
features.whatFallback: The add, search, commands, and finders buttons can float center-bottom, dock into either bottom corner, or stand as a vertical rail down the left edge.
features.howFallback: Pick a position under Config → Appearance → Button bar, or run :buttonbar from the command palette. The bar moves as you choose — no reload.
features.enableFallback: The side rail keeps the space under your bookmarks clear, which pays off on wide screens.

features.titleFallback: Shared bookmark form
features.whatFallback: Add and edit bookmarks in one centered modal — from the dashboard, Health, Inbox, Config, and search.
features.howFallback: Press +, Shift+B, or Ctrl+Shift+A to open the form. Use Create + New to save and immediately add another; the grid updates behind the modal.
features.enableFallback: Press ! for the full cheat sheet. Edit a row with ; or from Health and Inbox action bars.

features.titleFallback: GitHub update check
features.whatFallback: nextDash can compare your running version with GitHub once a day — a dot on ★, a toast while you are actively using the app, and a manual check in the ★ modal and Config → Overview.
features.howFallback: Press Check for updates in the ★ modal header or on Config → Overview. When a newer release exists, open GitHub from the notice or dismiss it until the next version.
features.enableFallback: On by default under Config → Behavior → Privacy. Turn off Check GitHub for new releases if you prefer no outbound request.

features.titleFallback: Bookmarks filters & search
features.whatFallback: Search, filter, and sort the full bookmark library from one list — with chips that show what is active and summary tiles that follow your filters.
features.howFallback: Type in the search box (shortcuts match too), pick page or category from the dropdowns, or click a page, category, or tag on a row. Sort by last opened, most opened, or pinned first. Tick rows for bulk favicon refresh or CSV export.
features.enableFallback: Open Config → Bookmarks. Scroll to load more rows; press o or double-click a row to open its URL.

features.titleFallback: Categories & tags first
features.whatFallback: Pages & tags now opens on Categories, with Tags right beside it — the two lists you reach for most often.
features.howFallback: Use [ and ] to cycle sub-tabs from anywhere in config, or click Categories or Tags in the strip. Pages, Finders, and Collections follow after.
features.enableFallback: Open Config → Pages & tags — Categories is selected by default.

features.titleFallback: Config keyboard navigation
features.whatFallback: Move through every config section, sub-tab, and list from the keyboard — no mouse required.
features.howFallback: Use j/k or arrow keys on the section rail, [ and ] for sub-tabs, and list keys on Pages & tags and Bookmarks. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K opens Find settings.
features.enableFallback: Press ! for the full cheat sheet, or open Help → Config navigation.

features.titleFallback: Find settings
features.whatFallback: Jump straight to any config section, sub-tab, help topic, or field you have visited.
features.howFallback: Press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K anywhere in config, or click Find settings below Help in the left nav. Type to filter, then Enter to go.
features.enableFallback: The shortcut works on every config section; the nav button is always below Help.

features.titleFallback: Page-scoped bookmark categories
features.whatFallback: Each page keeps its own category list. The Bookmarks filter shows only categories for the page you pick.
features.howFallback: Choose a page in the filter dropdown to scope categories and deep-link with #config/bookmarks/<pageId>. With All pages, categories show as Page · Category.
features.enableFallback: Open Config → Bookmarks and use the page filter at the top of the list.

features.titleFallback: Random theme
features.whatFallback: Let nextDash pick a different built-in theme from the pool instead of always showing your saved choice. Your saved theme remains the default whenever random is off.
features.howFallback: Choose Off (always your saved theme), On page refresh (new pick on each reload), or On view change (new pick when switching between bookmarks, config, inbox, health, or dashboard pages). With auto dark mode, only matching light or dark variants are eligible. While random is on, a Currently showing hint names the active theme.
features.enableFallback: Open Config → Appearance → Theme and set Random theme to the mode you want.
